supporting_evidence.finding: Patient on multiple antihypertensive agents with blood pressure at lower therapeutic limit
Elevated risk of orthostatic hypotension with intensive BP control

differential.reasoning: Intensive antihypertensive therapy in an obese, prediabetic patient can lower standing BP, predisposing to orthostatic symptoms; lack of orthostatic vitals makes this a leading but unconfirmed concern.

differential.reasoning: Combination of obesity, impaired glucose tolerance, and dyslipidemia fulfills criteria for metabolic syndrome, driving cardiovascular risk and informing management priorities.

primary_diagnosis: Hypertension overtreatment leading to orthostatic hypotension
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient’s profile of intensive antihypertensive therapy, obesity, prediabetes, and chronic anemia points to overtreatment of hypertension as the most likely driver of symptoms, especially orthostatic hypotension. Metabolic syndrome underlies the glucose and lipid abnormalities. Anemia lacks a defined cause and warrants work‑up. Obesity raises suspicion for OSA and early hypertensive kidney injury, while cardiovascular risk factors keep asymptomatic CAD and HFpEF on the differential, albeit with low likelihood. Gynecologic blood loss remains a remote possibility pending menstrual and iron studies.
unresolved_findings: High‑normal serum chloride (107.7 mmol/L) and CO₂ (28.9 mmol/L) – metabolic alkalosis not fully explained
Absence of eGFR, urine albumin‑creatinine ratio, and full renal panel
Missing complete blood count iron studies to classify anemia
No orthostatic vital signs or medication‑adherence assessment
Lack of sleep study or STOP‑BANG screening
No cardiac imaging (ECG, echocardiogram) or coronary calcium score
Missing thyroid function tests, vitamin D level, and liver panel
No documented menstrual history or pelvic imaging to evaluate gynecologic bleeding
recommended_workup: Measure orthostatic vital signs (supine and standing BP/HR)
Obtain comprehensive renal panel: serum creatinine, eGFR, urine albumin‑creatinine ratio
Order iron studies (serum ferritin, transferrin saturation), B12, folate
Screen for obstructive sleep apnea with STOP‑BANG and arrange polysomnography or home sleep test
Perform ECG and transthoracic echocardiogram to assess cardiac structure/function
Calculate 10‑year ASCVD risk and consider statin therapy per guidelines
Check thyroid panel (TSH, free T4) and vitamin D level
Review menstrual history; if heavy bleeding suspected, order pelvic ultrasound and consider gynecologic referral
